Proposals to improve a base model without iterative NONMEM runs

Source: R/nm_optimize_base.R
nm_optimize_base.Rd

Examines a base run and proposes changes to the residual error model, the random effects and the covariate model.

Usage

nm_optimize_base(
  run,
  covariates = NULL,
  deriv = NULL,
  nmfe_path = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  occ = NULL,
  level = 2L,
  cov_form = c("power", "exponential"),
  p_forward = 0.05,
  p_backward = 0.01,
  max_levels = 5L,
  objective = c("focei", "fast"),
  verbose = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'nm_optimize_base'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nm_optimize_base'
plot(x, type = c("all", "residual", "random", "covariate"), ...)

Arguments

run

Run directory (e.g. "run1.reg") or path prefix of the base run.

covariates

Covariates to test (columns of the data set). NULL: no covariate analysis.

deriv

Table written by the run of nm_derivatives_ctl() (<run>_deriv.dtab). NULL: searched for next to the run, otherwise the function runs level 1 only (unless nmfe_path is given).

nmfe_path

Path of nmfe: if given and no derivatives table exists, the derivatives control stream is written and run with nm_run().

data

Data set (path or data.frame) holding the covariates. Default: the $DATA file of the run.

occ

Occasion column for inter-occasion variability (level 2; it must be in the derivatives table: nm_derivatives_ctl(extra = "OCC")).

level

1 or 2 (2 runs both levels when the table is available).

cov_form

Form of continuous covariate effects: "power" ((COV/median)^theta) or "exponential" (exp(theta*(COV-median))).

p_forward, p_backward

Significance levels of the forward inclusion and backward elimination of covariates (linearized model).

max_levels

A numeric covariate with at most this number of distinct values is treated as categorical.

objective

Objective of the linearized model. "focei" (default): the FOCE-I objective of NONMEM with interaction (individual modes of the full individual objective, residual-variance term in the determinant); at the NONMEM estimates it reproduces the OFV of the base run. "fast": an approximation (modes given by the linear predictor with the residual variance held fixed), about three times faster, whose OFV differs from NONMEM's by a few units when the residual error depends on the ETAs; the dOFV are close.

verbose

Print progress.

x

An nm_optimize_base object.

...

Ignored.

type

For plot(): "all", "residual", "random" or "covariate". Formerly area, still accepted with a warning.

Value

An object of class nm_optimize_base: lists level1 (residual, random, pairs, covariates) and level2 (check, residual, random, covariates, scm, proposal), and proposal_text.

Details

Level 1 uses only the outputs of the base run (.phi, .ext, a table with CWRES, IPRED and TIME, and the data set): resmod-like models on the CWRES (power, time-varying, autocorrelated residuals, individual residual variance), EBE correlations, distribution and shrinkage, and an ETA-covariate screening.

Level 2 needs one extra NONMEM evaluation run written by nm_derivatives_ctl(). Its table of derivatives gives a first-order linearization of the model around the EBEs; every candidate is re-estimated in R under the FOCE-I objective of the linearized model: residual models (additive, proportional, combined, power, time-varying), OMEGA structure (full block, pairwise blocks, removal of an ETA, inter-occasion variability), covariates on the ETAs (univariate tests, then forward inclusion and backward elimination), and finally the combined proposal.

The changes in objective function (dOFV) are those of the linearized model: they approximate the changes of the real model, and the proposal must be confirmed by a NONMEM run of the modified model. The quality of the approximation is reported in check (linearized vs NONMEM OFV of the base model).

References

Khandelwal A, Harling K, Jonsson EN, Hooker AC, Karlsson MO. A fast method for testing covariates in population PK/PD models. AAPS J 2011;13:464-72. Ibrahim MMA, Nordgren R, Kjellsson MC, Karlsson MO. Model-based residual post-processing for residual model identification. AAPS J 2018;20:81.

See also

nm_derivatives_ctl(), nm_wasserstein()

Examples

ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", "run1.reg", package = "nmpilot")
o <- nm_optimize_base(ex, covariates = c("WT", "GENO"), level = 1, verbose = FALSE)
o
